Criterion: As applicable to the air vehicle, verify the performance of thrust reversers, speed brakes, and/or other auxiliary deceleration systems; and verify that there is no adverse loading or structural damage to the air vehicle when these devices are used. Standard: Auxiliary deceleration devices (alone or in combination with other deceleration devices) do not cause unacceptable air vehicle loadings or dynamics. Directional control of the air vehicle is maintained when these devices are in use for all specified operations, conditions, and expected environments. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses, tests and demonstrations. Design analysis verifies compliance at all operational and environmental conditions. Flight testing verifies the installation, functionality and performance capability of the thrust reversers and/or speed brakes and any other deceleration devices. Flight testing and demonstrations verify the absence of adverse effects on air vehicle control. References: AFGS-87139: 3.2.7.1 Arresting hook system; 3.2.7.2 Drag chutes

Standard: Auxiliary deceleration systems such as thrust reversers and speed brakes (alone or in combination with other deceleration systems as the main wheel braking) meet the stopping performance requirements and do not cause adverse loading, dynamics, or structural damage to the air vehicle. Directional control is maintained when auxiliary deceleration devices are used for all operations, conditions, and environments. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct a performance analysis to verify the auxiliary deceleration system is sized to provide the drag or thrust needed to decelerate the air vehicle to meet stopping distance requirements.
(2) Conduct analysis to verify the auxiliary deceleration system does not cause adverse loading, dynamics, or structural damage to the air vehicle. Test.
  (1) Ground test: Conduct ground test to verify that the auxiliary deceleration system meets the predicted performance (drag or thrust) to stop the air vehicle. The air vehicle maintains directional control and is not subjected to adverse loading, dynamics, or structural damage. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight testing to verify that the auxiliary deceleration system meets the predicted performance (drag or thrust) to stop the air vehicle. The air vehicle maintains directional control and is not subjected to adverse loading, dynamics, or structural damage.
